Yellow LEDs approximately 1.55 x 10^17 photons m-2 s-1, peak 585 nm (centroid 583 nm), the only visible light in the room. Beetles from a laboratory colony annually infused with wild insects from Beltsville, MD, USA; each beetle used once; 22 females and 22 males per series, naive control-period baselines n = 66 per sex; control periods used air alone. Upwind and downwind walking decreased relative to the control period (Wilcoxon signed-rank, p < 0.05 for the indexes); with four LEDs beetles showed no preference for any direction (Kruskal-Wallis, p > 0.05); sex differences in orientation not significant (p > 0.05); the abstract says orientation to the pheromone is abolished by low-intensity yellow light while the conclusion says diminished.
